why: rclrs validates a logger name against the rcutils rules and tracks whether that happened (`Validated` / `Unvalidated`), which is why its `Logger::new` returns `Result<Logger, RclrsError>`. Ours is `const fn Logger::new(&str) -> Self`, infallible, because a `Logger` must be constructible as a `static` in a `no_std` image -- `static LOGGER: nros_log::Logger = Logger::new("demo")` is the shape every embedded call site uses -- and a fallible constructor cannot initialise a `static`. What a user loses: an invalid logger name is accepted silently.
